pages.caption: Aegadian Islands Banner Levanzo.jpg · Simonetta Viterbi derivative work: Lkcl it · CC BY 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegadian_Islands_Banner_Levanzo.jpg
pages.text: The Aegadian Islands or Egadi Islands (Italian: Isole Egadi ) are a rugged cluster of islands set in turquoise waters 10 km off the western coast of Sicily, near Trapani and Marsala . They sit at the heart of the Egadi Islands Marine Protected Area, the largest marine reserve in the Mediterranean. The Aegadian Islands have been inhabited since prehistoric times. Cave paintings in Levanzo’s Grotta del Genovese show that humans lived here thousands of years ago. In 241 BC, the surrounding waters were the site of the Battle of the Aegates, where Rome defeated Carthage to end the First Punic War.

pages.caption: Aegadian Islands Banner Levanzo.jpg · Simonetta Viterbi derivative work: Lkcl it · CC BY 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegadian_Islands_Banner_Levanzo.jpg
pages.text: Over the centuries, the islands were ruled by Goths, Saracens, and Normans, who fortified Favignana in the 11th century. In the 1800s, they passed to the powerful Florio family, who industrialised tuna fishing — still part of island life today. Established in 1991, the Egadi marine reserve protects nearly 54,000 hectares of sea. It shelters Posidonia meadows, coral reefs, caves, and shipwrecks — home to dolphins, turtles, and the rare monk seal. Strict zoning balances conservation with fishing and tourism. Visitors can dive, snorkel, or join sea-watching tours — though some areas are off-limits to protect fragile habitats.

pages.caption: Aegadian Islands Banner Levanzo.jpg · Simonetta Viterbi derivative work: Lkcl it · CC BY 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegadian_Islands_Banner_Levanzo.jpg
pages.text: Most people speak standard Italian, and many in tourism know English, German, or French. Mobile coverage is good in villages, but internet access is limited — especially on Levanzo and Marettimo. Public Wi-Fi exists in Favignana, but connections can be unreliable elsewhere. Most visitors arrive via Trapani , the main gateway to the islands. You can fly into Trapani or Palermo airports, then travel to Trapani’s port for regular ferries and hydrofoils to all three islands. The crossing to Favignana takes as little as 30 minutes, with longer trips to Levanzo and Marettimo. Ferry and hydrofoil services vary by season, with more frequent departures in summer.

pages.caption: Levanzo, Egadi.jpg · Verbavolan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Levanzo,_Egadi.jpg
pages.text: Tickets can be bought at Trapani port or online. Arrive early in high season — evening returns especially can sell out. Liberty Lines – fast hydrofoils from Trapani to all three islands, plus routes from Marsala to Favignana and Marettimo The islands are best experienced on foot or by bike, especially Favignana, where a 33 km perimeter and gentle coastal roads make cycling the ideal way to explore. Bikes & e‑bikes rentals are available at ferry ports: about €10/day for a standard bike or €20 for an e‑bike.

pages.caption: Levanzo, Egadi.jpg · Verbavolan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Levanzo,_Egadi.jpg
pages.text: Scooters and small cars can be rented in Favignana; car access is restricted in summer, especially July–August. Taxis, a tourist train , and seasonal buses (Favignana only) cover key stops, though buses run infrequently and are timed seasonally. For sea‑focused island hopping, boat and dinghy rentals are also common, with informal boatmen offering grotto tours from the harbours. While most major sights are on the individual islands, the Aegadian Islands as a whole offer stunning coastal scenery, Mediterranean architecture, and historical remnants.

pages.caption: Levanzo, Egadi.jpg · Verbavolan · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Levanzo,_Egadi.jpg
pages.text: On Favignana , don’t miss the Ex Stabilimento Florio, a 19th-century tuna cannery turned museum that tells the story of the island’s industrial past. Levanzo is home to the Grotta del Genovese, a prehistoric cave with vivid Neolithic wall paintings and Paleolithic carvings — accessible only by guided tour. On Marettimo , you can hike to the Castello di Punta Troia, a restored Norman fortress perched dramatically above the sea, with sweeping views of the Egadi Marine Reserve. The Grotta del Genovese , on Levanzo , is one of the most significant archaeological sites in the Aegadian Islands, known for its Paleolithic and Neolithic cave paintings.

pages.caption: Favignana Cala Rossa 2 - panoramio (1).jpg · Arcona B&B · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Favignana_Cala_Rossa_2_-_panoramio_(1).jpg
pages.text: Natural landmarks such as Capo Grosso Lighthouse, sea stacks, and Byzantine chapels are scattered across the islands and usually reached on foot or by boat. The Aegadian Islands are made for outdoor exploration — whether by land or by sea. Swimming & Snorkelling – Crystal-clear waters, sea caves, and secluded coves make for unforgettable swims. Popular spots include Cala Rossa (Favignana), Cala Minnola (Levanzo), and Cala Bianca (Marettimo). Hiking – Levanzo and Marettimo offer rugged trails with spectacular views. Marettimo especially is known for challenging treks to lighthouses, remote chapels, and panoramic coastal bluffs. Boat Tours – Circumnavigate the islands to visit hidden grottoes, limestone cliffs, and monk seal habitats.

pages.caption: Favignana Cala Rossa 2 - panoramio (1).jpg · Arcona B&B · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Favignana_Cala_Rossa_2_-_panoramio_(1).jpg
pages.text: Day trips and sunset cruises depart regularly from each harbour. Diving – The Egadi Marine Protected Area harbours Roman wrecks, sea grass meadows, and underwater caves. Diving centres on Favignana and Marettimo offer guided dives for all levels. Excursions - Several local operators run day trips from Trapani, usually visiting two islands with stops for swimming and lunch aboard. Blu Lines – full-day cruises to Favignana, Levanzo, or Marettimo, with swimming stops and lunch on board. Also offers rental of small inflatable boats ("rubber ducks") for independent exploration. Escursione Favignana – offers private luxury dinghy tours, sailing trips, and full-day island cruises to Favignana, Levanzo, and Marettimo. Options include cave visits, swim stops, and onboard meals, with a focus on comfort and customisation. Prices are on the higher end.

pages.caption: Aegean Turkey banner.jpg · Pamukkale.jpg: CherryX derivative work: Inkey · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegean_Turkey_banner.jpg
pages.text: Aegean Turkey ( Turkish : Ege Bölgesi ) is the western part of Turkey bordering the Aegean Sea. It's bounded to the north by Marmara Region which includes Istanbul, to the south by the long coastline of Mediterranean Turkey , and east inland by the plateau of Central Anatolia which includes Ankara the capital. To the west and within sight are the East Aegean Islands of Greece. 1 Assos is a pleasant village with the Temple of Athena overlooking the sea. 8 Bodrum is a big resort with a castle built by the Knights Templar.

pages.caption: Aegean Turkey banner.jpg · Pamukkale.jpg: CherryX derivative work: Inkey · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegean_Turkey_banner.jpg
pages.text: 1 Aphrodisias is the ruin of an ancient city founded in honour of the goddess of love. 2 Dilek Peninsula National Park is the wildest stretch of this coast, with forests, hiking trails and desolate beaches. 3 Ephesus is the best preserved of Turkey's ancient cities, once the capital of Roman Asia Minor. Yet they were in Aegean Turkey all along. Edgar Allan Poe’s poem To Helen refers to Helen of Troy and the fleets of Nicaea , both a short distance north of this region, and modern visitors seeking the fabled ancient cities of Greece and Italy soon discover that the best-preserved are right here.

pages.caption: Aegean Turkey banner.jpg · Pamukkale.jpg: CherryX derivative work: Inkey · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegean_Turkey_banner.jpg
pages.text: Hellenistic and Roman culture spread by sea, since the alternative was to drag a pack-mule over arid hills. Aristotle and Homer lived and breathed here, Aegean olive oil was exported across the Med, and new concepts such as Christianity flourished – documented in 90 AD as the Seven Churches of Asia. Tourists began arriving 2000 years ago and today every few minutes another planeload flies in. This has led to a rash of mediocre development, but the best of the region still awaits you.

pages.caption: Assos.jpg · Gregorof at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Assos.jpg
pages.text: The climate is Mediterranean, with hot dry summers (daytime 30-35°C), warm transitional seasons that are often the best time to visit, and mild wet winters (daytime 10-15°C with 8-16 days of rain a month). Inland and mountain climate is more extreme, with sun-baked days over 35°C and biting cold winds, even snow, in winter. Turkish is obviously the main language, but English and German are widely understood in tourist facilities. By plane: the region’s airports are Izmir ( ADB ), Bodrum ( BJV ) and Dalaman ( DLM ). Frequent flights from Istanbul (IST) take an hour, plus daily from Istanbul (SAW), less often from other Turkish cities.

pages.caption: Assos.jpg · Gregorof at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Assos.jpg
pages.text: All of them in summer have flights from Europe, principally Britain, Germany and Russia: these are package-tours but offer flight-only tickets. By road: The main highways are fast, divided and in good repair. Mountain roads may be narrow and twisty, and treacherous in winter weather. Buses from Istanbul to Izmir depart hourly round the clock and take 8 hours, and buses converge on Izmir from Ankara, Konya and other major cities. So anywhere on these radial routes has a good service. Dolmuşes fill in the cross-country gaps, though they don’t always publish timetables, or even recognise the concept.

pages.caption: Assos.jpg · Gregorof at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 2.5 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Assos.jpg
pages.text: By train: the mountains are a major barrier to railways here. One daytime and one overnight train creak and groan from Ankara via Eskisehir (both on the high-speed line from Istanbul) to Izmir. You can also cross the Marmara Sea by ferry from Istanbul to Bandırma to connect with these trains at Balıkesir. An overnight train from Konya (also on the high-speed line) runs via Afyon and Manisa to Izmir. A regional train runs twice a day from Isparta to Izmir.

pages.caption: Bergama, Turkey.jpg · Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bergama,_Turkey.jpg
pages.text: By boat: Several Greek islands are close to the Turkish mainland and have ferry links: Lesvos to Ayvalik , Chios to Çeşme , Samos to Kuşadası , and Kos to Datça and Bodrum . These connect into the extensive Greek ferry network, so you can island-hop all the way from Piraeus the port for Athens. Buses connect the towns, but some major sites are at a distance from public transport. Consider hiring a car at your arrival airport. Day-trips to those sites are vigorously touted in the resorts, and solve the transport problem at the cost of trudging behind a green parasol all afternoon.

pages.caption: Bergama, Turkey.jpg · Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bergama,_Turkey.jpg
pages.text: You could negotiate a taxi for a few hours: this especially works for Priene, Didymus and Miletus, a scattered trio with poor signposting. It also helps at Ephesus and Pergamon where the natural route is to enter the uphill gate and tour through to the downhill gate, and the taxi driver will move to pick you up. Ancient cities: almost any town here has a 3000-year history, recounted in its municipal museum. By far the best are Ephesus and Pergamon , with other impressive sites at Assos , Miletus and Didyma .

pages.caption: Bergama, Turkey.jpg · Bernard Gagnon · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Bergama,_Turkey.jpg
pages.text: What you see today reflects a spate of Roman construction around 200 AD over earlier foundations: the state buildings and palaces at the core of a trading metropolis. (You’ll have to imagine the welter of smaller surrounding buildings that disappeared, and the port that dried up and caused the site to be abandoned.)

pages.caption: Aegina - Temple of Aphaia 03.jpg · Paweł 'pbm' Szubert (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegina_-_Temple_of_Aphaia_03.jpg
pages.text: Aegina (Greek: Αίγινα) is one of the Saronic Gulf Islands , a triangle 11 km on each side. It's the closest island to Athens, reached in barely an hour by ferry, and in 2011 had a population of 13,056. The main reasons to visit are to escape the city heat for an agreeable old port, and to see the temple of Aphaea. It feels more like a beach suburb than a Greek island, and it can get busy, but most visitors are from the city.

pages.caption: Aegina - Temple of Aphaia 03.jpg · Paweł 'pbm' Szubert (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegina_-_Temple_of_Aphaia_03.jpg
pages.text: Aegina is also the name of the main town and ferry port - and to avoid confusion it's referred to as "Aegina town" on this page. It's mainly geared for day-trippers, with some accommodation but lots of restaurants, and the Temple of Apollo is 500 m north. 1 Souvala (Σουβάλα) is the main village of the beach and resort strip along the north coast. 2 Agia Marina (Αγία Μαρίνα) is a small harbour on the east coast near the Temple of Aphaea. 3 Perdika (Πέρδικα) is a resort village near the south tip of the island.

pages.caption: Aegina - Temple of Aphaia 03.jpg · Paweł 'pbm' Szubert (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegina_-_Temple_of_Aphaia_03.jpg
pages.text: In legend Aegina was a goat-nymph, though it was almighty Zeus who acted the prize goat with his predatory sex adventures. Aegina was carried off to the island that now bears her name (maybe not unwillingly) and bore Zeus a son Aeacus, who became king. Hera the wife of Zeus tended to blame the other women rather than her hubby, and wiped out the island population by plague. However Aeacus prayed to Zeus to convert the teeming ants into humans, the myrmidons, a sort-of warrior caste - honestly, how many of us would have thought of doing that?

pages.caption: Aegina - Temple of Aphaia 03.jpg · Paweł 'pbm' Szubert (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aegina_-_Temple_of_Aphaia_03.jpg
pages.text: In the 7th to 5th centuries BC Aegina was a maritime trading state and its currency, embossed with a sea turtle and later a land tortoise, circulated widely in the Hellenistic world. Trade rivalry with Athens escalated into war, the island suffered a massacre in 424 BC, and this time the trick with the ants somehow couldn't be repeated. Aegina lost its importance and fell under the sway of other city-states, passing (as did Athens) into Roman, Byzantine, Venetian and Ottoman control. It has some agriculture but little industry, and has long been a holiday retreat for Athenians.

pages.caption: GR-aegina-orth-kirche.jpg · Bgabel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:GR-aegina-orth-kirche.jpg
pages.text: Frequent ferries ply from Piraeus port in Athens to Aegina town. Hydrofoils for foot passengers take 40 min, single fare €14, conventional vessels for cars and motorbikes take 70 min, single fare €10. Within the Piraeus port, follow signs for "Aegina" and "Gate E8" (to be sure, check the electronic screens, as specific gate can sometimes shift e.g., to E7). In normal times hydrofoils sail hourly 07:00-17:00, some continuing from Aegina to Agistri, Poros or Methana. The ferry operators are Hellenic Seaways , Blue Star Ferries and Saronic Ferries .

pages.caption: GR-aegina-orth-kirche.jpg · Bgabel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:GR-aegina-orth-kirche.jpg
pages.text: As of December 2025, Hellenic Seaways and Blue Star Ferries provide only hydrofoils option, while previouly mentioned Alpha Lines and ANES Ferries don't list Aegina in their schedules. 1 Aegina port is at the heart of the town. Ferries dock on the west pier, cruise ships on the east pier, and small craft use the inner harbour. There are lots of nearby cafes. There are five car rental agencies near the harbour, which also have motorbikes and scooters - book ahead to ensure availability. Some of their offerings are dilapidated. For a day trip, you might do better to hire a taxi.

pages.caption: GR-aegina-orth-kirche.jpg · Bgabel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:GR-aegina-orth-kirche.jpg
pages.text: The driver knows the roads, where to park and how much time to allow to return you to the ferry pier, and will regale you with what his great-grandmother got up to during the war. Buses on the island are a limited service to enable villagers to get into town for essentials then get home. They are not well-designed for sightseeing outings, but it's possible given boundless patience. The three routes all start from the bus stand by the harbour, and take at most 30 min to the end of the line. A single ticket is €2, pay cash as you board.

pages.caption: AphaeaTemple061.jpg · Martin451 · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AphaeaTemple061.jpg
pages.text: Destinations are only shown in Greek but if in doubt, get on and ask the driver. 1 Temple of Apollo ( Archaeology Museum ) ( 500 m north of harbour ). Fri-Mon, Wed 10:00-17:30 . Small museum and remains of a citadel on Kolona headland, you mostly come for the view. "Kolona" refers to the column, still standing, which was a daymark for approaching ships. Adult €4, conc €2, some free days . ( updated Apr 2020 )

pages.caption: AphaeaTemple061.jpg · Martin451 · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AphaeaTemple061.jpg
pages.text: Churches worth a look in town are St Nicholas Chapel (on west pier, the whitewashed building just as you step off the ferry), Isodia Theotokou (which you'll see even earlier from the boat, as it looms over the harbour), the Cathedral (on Mitropoleos) and Fanomeri (1 km inland and underground; it's often closed).

pages.caption: AphaeaTemple061.jpg · Martin451 · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AphaeaTemple061.jpg
pages.text: Landmarks and secular buildings in town are Government House (next to the cathedral, a modest 2-story building that in 1828/29 housed the newly independent Greek government until they could get set up in Athens), Eynardio (1830 building next to the cathedral), Tower of Markellos (a pink watchtower on Thomaidou) and the Kapodistrian Orphanage southside (looking uncannily like a prison, which it was).

pages.caption: Isole Eolie PagBan.jpg · forastico from Milano, Italia, FredTC · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Isole_Eolie_PagBan.jpg
pages.text: The Aeolian islands ( Italian : Isole Eolie , Sicilian: Ìsuli Eoli , Greek : Αιολίδες Νήσοι), aka Lipari Islands , are a group of attractive islands in the Tyrrhenian Sea about 25-50 km north of Sicily in Italy . This diverse group of volcanic islands used to be off the beaten track, but they are becoming more popular and can be very busy during July and August. The islands are inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List . Although local dialects of Sicilian are spoken among the locals, the traveller will find that standard Italian is also spoken by most people.

pages.caption: Isole Eolie PagBan.jpg · forastico from Milano, Italia, FredTC · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Isole_Eolie_PagBan.jpg
pages.text: Those involved in the tourist trade may also speak some English, German, or French. Cellular telephone coverage is dependable in the settled areas, but access to the internet is rare. There are a few internet cafes in Lipari Town. There are frequent car ferries and much quicker hydrofoils from Milazzo and Messina on Sicily , and from Reggio di Calabria on the mainland, to and between the islands. Most call first at Lipari, and then proceed to the other islands. Ferries are frequent in summer, with fewer during spring, autumn and winter and a reduced service year-round on Sundays.

pages.caption: Isole Eolie PagBan.jpg · forastico from Milano, Italia, FredTC · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Isole_Eolie_PagBan.jpg
pages.text: For timetables see SIREMAR , Ustica Lines and NGI . Check the timetables in advance, and allow plenty of time for connections, as boats can be early or late. A few car ferries a week also continue on to Naples (see SNAV ) and during the summer hydrofoils run from Naples , Cefalù , Palermo and Messina . The Aeolian Islands are quite remote, which is part of their appeal. No air travel is available to the archipelago, except for the very expensive helicopter service which runs during high season from the Catania airport. For more information see Air Panarea or HeliJet .

pages.caption: Aeolian islands.jpg · (WT-en) DanielC at WikiTravel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aeolian_islands.jpg
pages.text: Most international travellers, then, will arrive at the airport of either Palermo or Catania airport in Sicily, or Reggio di Calabria, across the straits of Messina on the mainland. The larger islands, Lipari , Vulcano and Salina have quite good bus services. Timetables are available at the tourist offices in each island's port. Those islands also have scooters for rent, and are the only of the islands with comprehensive systems of roads. Panarea and Stromboli are small enough to have no roads or automobiles to speak of; Panarea in particular is completely accessible by foot.

pages.caption: Aeolian islands.jpg · (WT-en) DanielC at WikiTravel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aeolian_islands.jpg
pages.text: Alicudi and Filicudi are so remote that they have little in the way of developed tourist industries or infrastructure. On those islands, transport from the port, and scooter rental, should be arranged with one's innkeeper. Boat rental is also popular for touring the periphery of each island; although the small boats for rent are not adequate for travel between the islands, but are popular for the excursion from Panarea to the islets of Basiluzzo and Drauto. Vulcano is the first port of call for ferries from Milazzo.

pages.caption: Aeolian islands.jpg · (WT-en) DanielC at WikiTravel · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aeolian_islands.jpg
pages.text: As well as the spectacular view of the narrow channel between this island and neighbouring Lipari, you're also greeted with the strange sight of a stack of sulphurous oozings, right by the harbour, with an accompanying smell! Disembarking, you can follow the road between that stack and a huge red rock, sulphurous fumes hissing out of the side of the pavement, to one of the island's main attractions. Next to the beach, the locals have created a hollow in the volcanic clay that is filled with yellow mud. After bathing in the mud, you can swim in the sea and wash it all off.

pages.caption: Aerial image of Stromboli (view from the northeast).jpg · Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aerial_image_of_Stromboli_(view_from_the_northeast).jpg
pages.text: Swimming here is a very special experience, because the fumaroles extend right out into the sea, bubbling up hot gas and giving the sensation of being in a jacuzzi, in the blue Mediterranean! The other main attraction on Vulcano is, you guessed it, the volcano! A steep climb from the town, you can walk to the summit of the island for a spectacular view of the other Aeolian Islands. If you have closed footwear, you can traverse the active vents on the north side of the main crater on your way to the top.

pages.caption: Aerial image of Stromboli (view from the northeast).jpg · Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aerial_image_of_Stromboli_(view_from_the_northeast).jpg
pages.text: Here, a great deal of steam and smelly gas is given off, and you can observe large sulphur crystals in the vents. Be careful not to burn your feet on the hot rocks and steam. Lipari is relatively pedestrian in comparison with exotic Vulcano. Fortunately, it has less exotic prices, and the large main town has a nice old quarter and a decent quota of non-tourist shops. Among the attractions on Lipari is the pumice quarry, reached from the main town by an infrequent bus service.

pages.caption: Aerial image of Stromboli (view from the northeast).jpg · Carsten Steger · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Aerial_image_of_Stromboli_(view_from_the_northeast).jpg
pages.text: This is right by the sea, and has a nice rocky beach where, interestingly, many of the rocks tend to float off into the sea! Stromboli is the most spectacular of the islands, as it's the only one that is volcanically active. In fact, it's the only volcano in the world that is known to have been continuously active throughout recorded history.

pages.caption: Band Amir banner.jpg · Afghanistan Matters https://www.flickr.com/photos/afgmatters/ · CC BY 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Band_Amir_banner.jpg
pages.text: Afghanistan is a landlocked country at the crossroads of Central and South Asia. The country shares borders with Uzbekistan , Turkmenistan , Tajikistan , Iran , Pakistan , China , and the disputed Kashmir territory. Once the centre of many powerful empires, the country has been in chaos and turmoil since the 1970s. Political unrest is rampant, and the country suffers from many social problems, such as war, drought, a public health crisis, terrorism, corruption, warlordism, poverty, and low literacy rates. However, under less extreme circumstances, this vast, mountainous country offers a lot to the adventurous, thrill-seeking traveller.

pages.caption: Band Amir banner.jpg · Afghanistan Matters https://www.flickr.com/photos/afgmatters/ · CC BY 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Band_Amir_banner.jpg
pages.text: Its landscapes are simply majestic, the history lover can appreciate numerous historical sites from all eras, and the architecture lover can feast their eyes on such wonderful Islamic architecture. There's even a shrine that houses a cloak once worn by Prophet Muhammad, the founder of Islam. Afghanistan is a melting pot of cultures, with Pashtuns, Tajiks, Hazaras, and Uzbeks constituting the largest ethnic groups. Islam is the state religion, hence the name "Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan". A majority of Afghans are Sunni Muslims, although about 20% of them are Shia Muslims.

pages.caption: Band Amir banner.jpg · Afghanistan Matters https://www.flickr.com/photos/afgmatters/ · CC BY 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Band_Amir_banner.jpg
pages.text: Agriculturally rich and traditionally a Muslim nation, Afghanistan is a mostly tribal society with each of the country's own subcultures in some specific regions. Despite poverty and political and religious extremism, tourists often find themselves being treated as celebrities here; in fact, they might be showered with a lot of hospitality and care, even if they unintentionally make a few cultural blunders. In the 1960s and early 1970s, Afghanistan was a popular destination for adventurous travellers, part of the "Hippie Trail" Istanbul to New Delhi overland route. Dirt cheap, culturally fascinating and with plenty of excellent hashish; what more could a hippie want?

pages.caption: Kabul TV Hill view.jpg · Sven Dirks, Wien · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kabul_TV_Hill_view.jpg
pages.text: However, it has not been anywhere close to safe since the Russian invasion of 1979. Since March 2026, the process for obtaining a tourist visa is quite easy for most travelers, as it can be obtained entirely online as an eVisa. Only a small number of countries, none of them Western, are restricted from this process. See the Get in section below for details. The south and east are predominantly Pushtun and the Hindu Kush mountain area has many Hazara, but all regions have considerable mixing of ethnic groups.

pages.caption: Kabul TV Hill view.jpg · Sven Dirks, Wien · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kabul_TV_Hill_view.jpg
pages.text: English spellings of Afghan place names vary as there is no regulation of names when written in the Latin script. For example, Q may replace K as in Qandahar or Qunduz. The Taliban destroyed the irrigation systems and it is just beginning to recover. 8 Wakhan National Park – one of Afghanistan's most isolated areas, with soaring mountains and unique culture Afghanistan has been in the news since the late 1970s for all the wrong reasons. While visiting has not been advisable for many years, it has much to offer the intrepid traveller. However, even the more adventurous tourists should consider looking elsewhere for thrill-seeking. Afghanistan borders Persia , Central Asia and South Asia , and various Silk Road routes cross it to connect those regions. It has been described as "the crossroads of Asia" and has history of trade going back to before 2000 BCE. Human presence in the fertile river valleys dates back tens of thousands of years.

pages.text: Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected wildlife area in Boki Local Government Area of Cross River State , Nigeria . It protects approximately 100 km² of lowland and submontane forest around the Afi Mountains and is an important refuge for endangered wildlife, including the Cross River gorilla, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, and drill. The sanctuary is also known for its birdlife, mountain scenery, hiking opportunities and the nearby Drill Ranch, a wildlife rehabilitation and conservation project. Afi Mountain is listed as an Important Bird Area in Nigeria, and the area contains a major roost for migratory European barn swallows.

pages.caption: Pagebanner default.jpg · Derivative work by john2690. Other authors listed on source image page. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pagebanner_default.jpg
pages.text: Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary was established in May 2000 from part of the former Afi River Forest Reserve. It is managed by the Cross River State Forestry Commission, with conservation and research support from organisations including the Wildlife Conservation Society and Pandrillus. The sanctuary covers lowland and submontane rainforest, with rocky mountain peaks reaching approximately 1,300 metres. It forms part of a wider forest landscape that connects with the Mbe Mountains and other important wildlife habitats in the Cross River region. Afi is particularly important for the conservation of the Cross River gorilla, one of the world's most endangered great apes.

pages.caption: Pagebanner default.jpg · Derivative work by john2690. Other authors listed on source image page. · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pagebanner_default.jpg
pages.text: Other important species include the Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, drill and grey-necked rockfowl. Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary consists mainly of tropical lowland and sub-montane forest, with rocky peaks rising to about 1,300 m. The sanctuary is an important habitat for several endangered species, including the critically endangered Cross River gorilla, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee, drill and grey-necked rockfowl. The forest contains a wide variety of tree species, including Parkia bicolor , Pycnanthus angolensis , Albizia zygia , Monodora myristica and Irvingia gabonensis . Open areas created by dry-season fires are quickly colonised by herbaceous plants, which provide an important food source for gorillas.

pages.caption: View from Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary.jpg · Dotun55 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:View_from_Afi_Mountain_Wildlife_Sanctuary.jpg
pages.text: Other wildlife found in the sanctuary includes red river hogs, bushbucks and several species of monkeys. The western side of the mountain also contains an important roost for migratory European barn swallows, which can number in the millions during the wintering season. Afi Mountain has a humid tropical climate, with a distinct rainy season and a drier period during the year. The area receives heavy rainfall, with annual rainfall generally ranging from about 3,000 to 3,800 mm. The rainy season usually lasts from around March or April to September, while the drier season generally occurs from October to March.

pages.caption: View from Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary.jpg · Dotun55 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:View_from_Afi_Mountain_Wildlife_Sanctuary.jpg
pages.text: Temperatures are generally warm throughout the year, although the mountainous terrain produces cooler conditions at higher elevations. During the rainy season, heavy rainfall can make roads and hiking trails difficult to use. Visitors planning to hike should be prepared for wet conditions and bring suitable rain gear and sturdy footwear. Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary is in Boki Local Government Area of Cross River State. The sanctuary is reached through the surrounding communities, with access to the mountain and conservation facilities arranged locally. Visitors planning to hike the mountain should make arrangements in advance with the conservation project or local guides.

pages.caption: View from Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary.jpg · Dotun55 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:View_from_Afi_Mountain_Wildlife_Sanctuary.jpg
pages.text: Pandrillus advises visitors to contact Drill Ranch before travelling because road conditions and access can change. Fees for visiting Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary may vary. Drill Ranch's visitor information page lists fees from November 2019, but these may no longer be current. A guide is required for hikes into Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary. Day hikes and multi-day treks can be arranged through Drill Ranch, with additional fees collected on behalf of the Cross River State Forestry Commission. Visitors should contact Drill Ranch in advance to confirm the current fees, guide charges and any required permissions before travelling.

pages.caption: Water course, Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary, Cross River State.jpg · Charles Emogor · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Water_course,_Afi_Mountain_Wildlife_Sanctuary,_Cross_River_State.jpg
pages.text: Fees may vary for student groups and other organised groups. The sanctuary is a protected area, so visitors must follow the instructions of the Forestry Commission, guides and conservation staff. Birdwatching is permitted, but mist-netting is not allowed except by special arrangement with the state wildlife authority. Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary is a rugged mountainous area with steep canyons, ridges and forest trails. There are no regular public transport services within the sanctuary. Visitors exploring the sanctuary must be accompanied by a guide. Day hikes and multi-day treks can be arranged through Drill Ranch at Afi Mountain.

pages.caption: Water course, Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary, Cross River State.jpg · Charles Emogor · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Water_course,_Afi_Mountain_Wildlife_Sanctuary,_Cross_River_State.jpg
pages.text: For longer hikes, visitors should be physically fit and carry suitable hiking equipment, food and drinking water. Within the Drill Ranch area, the animal enclosures and forest attractions are reached on foot along winding paths. Motorcycles can be used to reach the area from nearby villages, while some sections of the access road may require a four-wheel-drive vehicle, particularly during the rainy season. Visitors should contact Drill Ranch in advance before travelling, as road conditions can change and access arrangements may vary. The sanctuary is home to populations of Cross River gorillas, Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzees, drills and other forest wildlife. Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed, as many of the animals are shy and live in dense forest.

pages.caption: Dust Cloud Etosha National Park banner.jpg · User:Yathin sk · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dust_Cloud_Etosha_National_Park_banner.jpg
pages.text: Africa is the wellspring of the human race. The second largest continent in the world in both area and population, it offers the visitor a unique blend of natural wonders, renowned prehistoric sites, numerous and often sprawling remains of several of the world's greatest ancient civilisations, vibrant cultures, remote villages, and modern cities. Africa has shorelines on the Indian Ocean to the southeast, the Atlantic Ocean to the west, the Red Sea to the northeast, the Gulf of Aden slightly further south, and the Mediterranean Sea to the north.

pages.caption: Dust Cloud Etosha National Park banner.jpg · User:Yathin sk · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dust_Cloud_Etosha_National_Park_banner.jpg
pages.text: This huge continent is more than 8,000 km (5,000 mi) across north-south and 7,500 km (4,800 mi) east-west with some islands even further out and contains many vastly different peoples, religions, and cultures. Africa has more than 50 sovereign countries—the most of any continent. Africa's Nile River is claimed by some to be the longest river in the world (other geographers argue that the Amazon is longer); the Nile runs 6,650 km (over 4,100 mi) from Burundi to Egypt .

pages.caption: Dust Cloud Etosha National Park banner.jpg · User:Yathin sk · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Dust_Cloud_Etosha_National_Park_banner.jpg
pages.text: The Congo River in the DR Congo is the second largest in terms of discharge, and the deepest with a depth of over 230 m (750 ft) in some spots. Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the world's tallest free-standing mountain at 5,890 m (19,340 ft). Lake Assal in Djibouti is the second-lowest point on Earth, the saltiest lake outside Antarctica , and one of the hottest places on Earth. While the first activity most people associate with Africa is safaris , there are endless possibilities for adventure.

pages.caption: Accra town.jpg · Goldenwabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Accra_town.jpg
pages.text: For example, you can purchase crafts in markets, venture into the Sahara with a Tuareg caravan, visit traditional villages, hike through the jungle to watch gorillas, climb mountains with rugged landscapes and icy peaks, snorkel in the numerous marine parks while feeding fish, relax on tropical islands in the Indian and Atlantic Oceans, snack on exotic treats, paddle down a river in a dugout pirogue or travel across savanna on a colonial-era railway.

pages.caption: Accra town.jpg · Goldenwabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Accra_town.jpg
pages.text: Africa's cultural diversity cannot be overstated — most countries are internally diverse and there are huge differences between the Muslim countries in the north with their Arab- and Berber-influenced cultures and the sub-Saharan nations, including the rainbow nation of South Africa that has strong European influences in addition to Bantu and other African traditions. It is also the continent with the largest genetic diversity among the population by far: There is far more genetic diversity among Africans than there is between Africans and inhabitants of any other continent.

pages.caption: Accra town.jpg · Goldenwabbit · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Accra_town.jpg
pages.text: Despite what lacking media coverage might have led you to believe, Africa is not one country but over 50 countries, making it impossible to make generalisations about "all of Africa". Partly also due to the nature of colonial borders, most African countries are anything but homogeneous (for example, South Africa has 11 official languages), and culture, cuisine, language, or even the dominant religion may change dramatically within a few hundred kilometres without ever crossing a border. Despite rapidly growing economies in many places, there are still many pockets of poverty in both the Maghreb and sub-Saharan Africa.

pages.caption: AddisView.jpg · DaneyWiki · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AddisView.jpg
pages.text: While poverty, corruption, and ethnic and religious violence exist in some parts of the continent, large parts of Africa have made impressive progress, with many cities that have growing middle classes and deal with problems such as traffic jams and crowded public transport, rather than the war or famine you might have heard about in some 1980s documentary or development aid commercial. Most people outside the continent divide Africa into two regions: the Arabic-speaking North Africa, and everywhere else as sub-Saharan Africa. However, Africa is a very diverse continent, and this division represents a somewhat shallow understanding.

pages.caption: AddisView.jpg · DaneyWiki · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AddisView.jpg
pages.text: 2 Addis Ababa — Ethiopia's capital is one of Africa's "global cities" as a seat of the African Union and of many non-government organisations. 3 Cairo — Egypt's bustling capital is the most populous city in North Africa and a gateway to the heritage of Ancient Egypt. 4 Cape Town — the Mother City of South Africa with Table Mountain, the Cape of Good Hope, and numerous other attractions. 6 Johannesburg — South Africa's largest city and perhaps the continent's key financial and economic centre. 7 Luanda — Angola's capital and largest city, which has been through a huge renaissance in the past decade.

pages.text: 9 Nairobi — the capital of Kenya, the largest city in East and Central Africa, and home to the only UN agency headquarters outside of Europe and the U.S. 1 Axum (Aksum) — the ancient capital of Ethiopia, famous for the ruins of various palaces and its stelae 2 Dogon Country — a region of south-central Mali renowned for its secluded villages embedded on cliffs and a very distinct culture 4 Leptis Magna — intended by the Roman Empire as a model city, its ruins are still impressive

pages.caption: African-American-history.jpg · Yoichi Okamoto · Public domain · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:African-American-history.jpg
pages.text: African-American history is a travel topic about the history of American people of African descent. The Atlantic Slave Trade that existed from the 1500s to the 1800s resulted in many Africans being taken from Africa and being brought to the Americas as slaves. Some of the slaves were taken to what is today the United States , where slavery continued in the South until the American Civil War of the 1860s, after which slavery, except as a punishment for a crime, was outlawed throughout the United States.

pages.caption: African-American-history.jpg · Yoichi Okamoto · Public domain · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:African-American-history.jpg
pages.text: During the entire period of chattel slavery in the U.S., there was also a smaller number of free black citizens, and some of them played very important roles in U.S. history, including Crispus Attucks, who, as the first victim of the Boston Massacre, can be thought of as the first casualty of the Revolutionary War that brought the U.S. into being. Many of these free black people even had slaves of their own.

pages.caption: African-American-history.jpg · Yoichi Okamoto · Public domain · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:African-American-history.jpg
pages.text: However, after the end of post-Civil War Reconstruction, various states, especially in the South, instituted segregation and Jim Crow laws, effectively denying black citizens the right to vote and largely separating blacks and whites in any situation where they might otherwise be treated equally. Even in the North, which did not have formal segregation laws, most places were segregated in practice, with many fancier establishments barring entry to non-white patrons. Things would get worse with the rise of the automobile, when suburban homes were largely restricted to white residents, and non-white people were largely forced to live in blighted inner-city neighborhoods.

pages.caption: PreservationHallClosed2.jpg · Infrogmation · CC BY 2.5 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PreservationHallClosed2.jpg
pages.text: It was not until the Civil Rights Movement gained steam again in the 1950s-1960s that such practices were eventually outlawed and overturned, and not until 2008 that an African-American would be elected president; see postwar United States for context. Despite the discrimination they have faced since the 17th century, African Americans have made tremendous contributions in every field. To take one example, it's nearly impossible to imagine what American music might sound like without the inventiveness, excellence, and unique heritage of African-American musicians. To take another, it is probably impossible to imagine what Southern cuisine would be like without the creativity of African-American cooks.

pages.caption: PreservationHallClosed2.jpg · Infrogmation · CC BY 2.5 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PreservationHallClosed2.jpg
pages.text: African-American soldiers also made valuable contributions in the Civil War, Spanish-American War, and both world wars, despite being forced to serve in segregated units. The wars, in turn, had a huge influence on African-American history, with the Civil War leading to the end of slavery and a short period of African-American political ascendancy in the South, but the mere experience of white soldiers fighting the same battles as their black brothers-in-arms converted some staunch racists into advocates of black civil rights. This can be particularly observed in diaries, memoirs, and letters home of white northern Civil War soldiers.

pages.caption: PreservationHallClosed2.jpg · Infrogmation · CC BY 2.5 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PreservationHallClosed2.jpg
pages.text: Similarly, returning soldiers after both world wars who had experienced a slightly less discriminatory world in the trenches and on the battlefields were not willing to put up with Jim Crow segregation — especially after the Second World War, a war they'd been told was about defeating racism. In the days of segregation and well into the 1970s, due to being largely excluded from mainstream white spaces, African-Americans developed an entire separate musical infrastructure consisting of live performance venues, radio stations, television stations, and record companies, often known as the Chitlin Circuit.

pages.caption: African National Monument-1.jpg · Rodney Leon · Public domain · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:African_National_Monument-1.jpg
pages.text: Many top African-American musical talents like Michael Jackson, Lionel Richie, Diana Ross and Peabo Bryson, and even the odd white performer like Teena Marie, honed their craft through this musical infrastructure, developing a distinctly African-American sound, though they were severely underpaid compared to their white counterparts. It was not until the 1980s that African-American stars were able to have a powerful enough negotiating position for Michael Jackson to become the highest earning pop singer of all time. With increasing racial integration, this distinct African-American music circuit largely disappeared by the 1990s, having been mostly absorbed into the mainstream corporate music industry.

pages.caption: African National Monument-1.jpg · Rodney Leon · Public domain · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:African_National_Monument-1.jpg
pages.text: A Black Bostonian named Crispus Attucks was killed by British forces in the "Boston Massacre" that helped trigger the American Revolution. Boston was subsequently an abolitionist stronghold and a target for the Underground Railroad . In music, the modern boyband concept was pioneered in the 1980s by the African-American group New Edition, whose members were from Boston; their style would inspire later groups like New Kids on the Block, Boyz II Men, Backstreet Boys, and N'Sync. The South Side of Chicago was once home to Black Metropolis, an economically thriving area with many black-owned businesses.

pages.caption: African National Monument-1.jpg · Rodney Leon · Public domain · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:African_National_Monument-1.jpg
pages.text: Sadly, the advent of redlining and blockbusting in the postwar years led to the decline of the area, and these days, the South Side has a partly-deserved reputation for high violent crime rates. That said, don't write off a visit to the area entirely, as there are strong upper and middle-class black neighborhoods that are perfectly safe to visit, and Bronzeville, the historical heart of the Black Metropolis, is quickly gentrifying due to the influx of upwardly mobile black millennials.

They can be visited for safaris , to see the African flora and fauna . 19 Sehlabathebe National Park — remote mountain reserve great for hiking with rare wildlife, impressive waterfalls, and ancient rock paintings and stone shelters 20 Ts'ehlanyane National Park — the largest national park in Lesotho: rugged wilderness at a high altitude 22 Lake Malawi National Park — famous for its incredibly high level of diversity in fish species 30 Bwabwata National Park — Composed by ex "Caprivi Game Park" and ex "Mahango Game Reserve".

Also crosses into Uganda where it is known as Mgahinga Gorilla National Park

pages.text: South Africa is home to a vast array of national parks – see South African national parks for coverage of South Africa. 61 Serengeti National Park — huge national park in Tanzania , perhaps the archetypal African game park; becomes the Maasai Mara National Reserve over the border in Kenya 67 Rwenzori National Park — home of the almost mythical, otherworldly scenery of the Mountains of the Moon in Uganda 74 Luambe National Park — used to be the president's private game reserve, now pristine wilderness without mass tourism 76 Nsumbu National Park — used to be very popular in the 1970s but has declined in the last decades 82 Hwange National Park (formerly Wankie Game Reserve) — the largest natural reserve in Zimbabwe, at 14,600 km²

pages.caption: Safari Kenya banner.jpg · User:Cmocho · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Safari_Kenya_banner.jpg
pages.text: African flora and fauna is a highlight of trips to Africa , especially on visits to the continent's national parks . Going on a safari is a common way to see it. Most of Africa is part of the Afrotropical realm , together with the southern Arabian peninsula and a small part of Iran. North Africa is part of the Palearctic realm , and contains Eurasian wildlife . The wildlife of Madagascar differs a lot from the mainland, and is described in a separate article.

pages.caption: Safari Kenya banner.jpg · User:Cmocho · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Safari_Kenya_banner.jpg
pages.text: Many safari visitors are keen on seeing the Big Five — buffalo, elephant , leopard, lion and rhino — but there is a lot more out there if you know where to look. Africa is home to an extremely wide variety of primates, including all the extant great apes except the orangutan. Modern humans are also believed by most scientists to trace their origins to Africa. Papio ursinus , also known as the common baboon , lives in social groups guided by a dominant male. Newborn baboons are black and are carried around by their mothers.

pages.caption: Safari Kenya banner.jpg · User:Cmocho · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Safari_Kenya_banner.jpg
pages.text: Later, they ride on the back of their mother and after three to four months they change color to the adult brown-grey. The mandrill is ( Mandrillus sphinx ) is known for its distinctive colourful face. Males are noticeably larger and more brightly-coloured than females. Females and their juvenile offspring usually live in large groups called hordes that can number up to several hundred, while adult males are usually solitary, only approaching hordes during the mating season. Alpha males are recognisable by their brightly-coloured posteriors.

pages.caption: ChacmaBaboon Walking.JPG · (WT-en) Jpatokal at English Wikivoyage · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ChacmaBaboon_Walking.JPG
pages.text: The bonobo ( Pan paniscus ), formerly known as the "pygmy chimpanzee", is an endangered great ape closely related to the chimpanzee, with both species being humans' closest living relatives. Like its slightly more robust cousin, its diet consists mostly of fruit, though it supplements its diet with eggs, meat, honey, and insects. It's found exclusively in the Congo Basin, separated from the range of the chimpanzee by the Congo and Kasai Rivers. Because of their jungle habitat and timid nature, bonobos are rarely seen in the wild. The main threats to the species are habitat disruption, the bushmeat trade, and ongoing wars in the region.

pages.caption: ChacmaBaboon Walking.JPG · (WT-en) Jpatokal at English Wikivoyage · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ChacmaBaboon_Walking.JPG
pages.text: The chimpanzee ( Pan troglodytes ), while more numerous than the bonobo, is also listed as endangered. There are four recognized subspecies (with a fifth proposed), with one living in coastal West Africa and the others to the north and east of the Congo River in Central Africa. Unlike the bonobo, which prefers rainforests, it can adapt to habitats ranging from open savanna to thick rainforests. They're easier to spot than bonobo, as they're less timid and can more often be found in open environments. The main threats to chimps are similar to those faced by bonobo, and also include infectious diseases that may also affect humans.

pages.caption: ChacmaBaboon Walking.JPG · (WT-en) Jpatokal at English Wikivoyage · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:ChacmaBaboon_Walking.JPG
pages.text: Gorillas are divided into two species: eastern ( Gorilla beringei ) and western ( Gorilla gorilla ). Both are endangered, and both are only found (in the wild) in poor African countries. The most practical way of seeing gorillas in the wild is through organized tours in Rwanda or Uganda . To see western gorillas, the Republic of the Congo appears to be the best option. Outside of these organized tours/treks, not only do you have to get very lucky to see a gorilla, but you may have to deal with dangers both natural and human.

pages.caption: Mandrils (36370557765).jpg · Eric de Redelijkheid from Utrecht, Netherlands · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mandrils_(36370557765).jpg
pages.text: Cercopithecus aethiops is a social monkey that lives close to rivers and feeds on leaves, fruits and insects. Family groups are up to 20 members strong. Newborn vervet monkeys are dependent on their mothers for three months, and from then on they become youngsters. Cheetahs ( Acinonyx jubatus ) are the fastest hunters in Africa, but you are quite lucky if you can see them very close because they tend to be hidden in the high grass. You don't see them in the dense thickets of South Africa whereas the savanna in Kenya and Tanzania allows for better viewing.

pages.caption: Mandrils (36370557765).jpg · Eric de Redelijkheid from Utrecht, Netherlands · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mandrils_(36370557765).jpg
pages.text: Cheetahs usually travel alone or in small groups consisting of the mother and her offspring. They hunt in the cool hours of the day. Cheetahs reach a maximum speed of up to 100 km/h in a short and explosive burst, and tackle their prey in a single attack. The preferred prey is Impala, but birds are on the menu as well. Panthera pardus are famously elusive hunters that stalk their prey at night.

pages.caption: Mandrils (36370557765).jpg · Eric de Redelijkheid from Utrecht, Netherlands · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mandrils_(36370557765).jpg
pages.text: For most visitors, the only chance of spotting one is on night drives, and Zambia's South Luangwa National Park (which allows night driving) is claimed by some to have the highest density of leopards in all of Africa. Panthera leo are common in the wider part of Africa and can be best seen in Lake Nakuru National Park , Masai Mara National Park , Serengeti and to a lesser extent in South Africa, nevertheless you have to be lucky to see them very close.

pages.caption: Afrikaans phrasebook WV banner.jpg · Missvain Original author: User:Wajahatmr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afrikaans_phrasebook_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: Afrikaans is spoken throughout South Africa and Namibia . The language is mainly derived from Dutch but has been influenced by the Malay language . However, most Afrikaans speakers in the workplace have some knowledge of English and increasingly, those who have studied at a tertiary-level establishment are instructed in English. Note that Afrikaans pronunciation is extremely difficult and can be a challenge, even for Dutch speakers. In some loan words, 'g', 'v' and 'w' may be pronounced the same as their English equivalents, but this is uncommon.

pages.caption: Afrikaans phrasebook WV banner.jpg · Missvain Original author: User:Wajahatmr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afrikaans_phrasebook_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: Like English, double consonants in Afrikaans are pronounced as a single sound, and not two separate sounds, unless occurring at a syllabary break: 'wekker': 'vack-er' (alarm clock) but 'melkkoei': 'melk-koo-ee' (milking cow). Note that although Afrikaans digraphs and trigraphs contain mostly vowels and sound as though they contain many syllables, they in fact are seen as a single syllable. For example, the word 'Goeie' sounds as if it contains 3 syllables, but in fact contains only two: 'goei' and 'e' are the 2 syllables. From this, you can see Afrikaans pronunciation, like English for a foreigner, can be rather irregular.

pages.caption: Afrikaans phrasebook WV banner.jpg · Missvain Original author: User:Wajahatmr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afrikaans_phrasebook_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: Pronunciation can be hard and the accent is extremely difficult to master, but when spoken correctly, Afrikaans is the most melodic Germanic language. However, one should not be daunted. Afrikaans grammar is really quite simple and is more similar to English than to any other Germanic language. Verbs are even simpler than English: there is no am or are or were but only is and was . One who is learning Afrikaans will probably catch onto it rather quickly and will have no problem with speaking Dutch or understanding German .

pages.caption: Afrikaans phrasebook WV banner.jpg · Missvain Original author: User:Wajahatmr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afrikaans_phrasebook_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: When new concepts are developed, the Dutch will often adapt the English word whereas the Afrikaaners will invent their own word. Thus the Afrikaans word will make sense to a Dutch-speaker even though the Dutch-speaker themselves would not use the word. For example, the Dutch use the word the lift (the same word as is used in Britain) for an "elevator", while in Afrikaans, one would use the word hysbak ( hys meaning "to raise" and bak meaning a "container"). A rukkie in Afrikaans is a short period of time, not a sexual act performed on oneself.

pages.caption: Afrikaans phrasebook WV banner.jpg · Missvain Original author: User:Wajahatmr · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afrikaans_phrasebook_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: Common use examples are Ek gaan 'n rukkie slaap or Ek sal oor 'n rukkie daar wees Certain words in Afrikaans are also derived from Malay and might therefore not be understood by Dutch speakers. Such words include "baklei ("fight" or in Dutch "vecht"), "piesang" ("banana" or in Dutch "banaan") and "baie" ("many" or in Dutch "veel"), though the word "veel" is also widely used in Afrikaans. Dutch does not use the "double negative" whereas Afrikaans does - for example "You must not do it" becomes J y moe nie dit doen nie in Afrikaans while in Dutch it becomes Je mag het niet doen.

pages.caption: AfyonKarahisar Kalesi - panoramio (cropped).jpg · Emin Başar ÖZDEMİR · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AfyonKarahisar_Kalesi_-_panoramio_(cropped).jpg
pages.text: Afyonkarahisar or Afyon is a city in Central Anatolia 250 km southwest of Ankara, with a population in 2020 of 245,405. Its fortress or citadel perches on a black volcanic crag, an obvious defensive position. The area is dotted with similar volcanic plugs, and underground heat makes this a geothermal area, with many hotel spas. These and the collection of mosques around the foot of the citadel are the main reason to visit. Afyon - kara - hisar literally means "opium black fortress".

pages.caption: AfyonKarahisar Kalesi - panoramio (cropped).jpg · Emin Başar ÖZDEMİR · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AfyonKarahisar_Kalesi_-_panoramio_(cropped).jpg
pages.text: This is a large growing area for opium poppies - the open fields have been burned out to curb the illegal trade but production continues under tight control for medicinal opiates such as morphine. Afyon produces fine marble, the Docimian Pavonazzetto variety being white with purple veins. The quarries are ugly places and the best place to admire the marble is in the many grand buildings it has gone to adorn, such as the Pantheon and St Peter's in Rome, and Hagia Sophia in Istanbul. In 2004 the Turkish parliament decided it didn't like having a city called Opium (maybe too much confusion with YSL perfume?)

pages.caption: AfyonKarahisar Kalesi - panoramio (cropped).jpg · Emin Başar ÖZDEMİR · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AfyonKarahisar_Kalesi_-_panoramio_(cropped).jpg
pages.text: and changed the name to Afyonkarahisar. "Afyon" is what it remains locally and on this page, but you might want to give it the full name when explaining your travel plans to border guards. Buses from Istanbul run every hour or two, taking 7 hours via Gebze , Izmit , Adapazarı and Kütahya , for a fare in 2022 of 230 TL. Some continue to Antalya or Konya . Buses from Ankara run every 30 min, taking 3 hr 30 min via Polatlı for a fare of 180 TL. Some continue to Izmir , another 5 hours.

pages.caption: Afyonkarahisar Kalesi havadan.jpg · Nabbegat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afyonkarahisar_Kalesi_havadan.jpg
pages.text: 1 Otobüs Terminali is the bus station just off the bypass 3 km northwest of town centre. It's modern and spacious with cafes and shops, and long-distance buses often take a rest stop here. Take a taxi or dolmuş to get downtown. Konya Mavi Tren runs daily from Konya at 19:00 to reach Afyon shortly after 23:00. It trundles on through the night via Uşak and Manisa to reach Izmir by 07:30. The eastbound train leaves Izmir towards 20:00 to reach Afyon at 04:30 and Konya at 08:30.

pages.caption: Afyonkarahisar Kalesi havadan.jpg · Nabbegat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afyonkarahisar_Kalesi_havadan.jpg
pages.text: A regional train runs from Eskişehir at 17:45 via Kütahya to reach Afyon by 21:00; the return train leaves Afyon at 07:30. Two other trains down this line only run as far as Kütahya, and trains no longer continue from Afyon to Konya. A YHT line under construction towards Izmir may one day bring high speed trains from Istanbul and Ankara. 2 Afyon Ali Çetinkaya is the town railway station, an Art Deco structure of 1939 named for the minister of transportation of that era. It's 1 km northwest of the castle.

pages.caption: Afyonkarahisar Kalesi havadan.jpg · Nabbegat · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Afyonkarahisar_Kalesi_havadan.jpg
pages.text: Şehir Garı (City Station) 1 km west off Atatürk Blv was the terminus of trains from Izmir until it closed in 2017. The area has been redeveloped for industry, so its Ottoman chalets have been swept away. From Istanbul follow O-7 east onto O-5 then O-22. Continue on D200 via İnegöl and Bozüyük, then D650 / D230 south past Kütahya. AFRAY is a city suburban railway under construction. There's no word on when it might open. It perches atop the crag above the town. It was built by the Hittites in 1350 BC and rebuilt several times since.

pages.caption: VictoryMuseumAfyonkarahsar.JPG · CeeGee · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:VictoryMuseumAfyonkarahsar.JPG
pages.text: It's reached by a 226 m climb up some 800 steps, starting from the southwest on Kale Cd above Ulu Camii; the project to build a cable-car has stalled. The site is open 24 hours free and has extensive citadel walls, cisterns and views but not much else within except trash. 2 Ulu Camii (Great Mosque) near the start of the castle ascent was completed in 1277. Its roof is supported by an array of 8 by 5 wooden pillars that were originally richly carved. It's one of five world heritage listed wooden mosques in Anatolia. 3 Sultan Dîvânî Mevlevîhâne Museum , Zaviye Türbe Cd .

pages.caption: VictoryMuseumAfyonkarahsar.JPG · CeeGee · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:VictoryMuseumAfyonkarahsar.JPG
pages.text: A lodge for the Mevlevi, the Sufi "whirling dervishes", now a museum. 4 Sülüm Mosque on Birlik Cd north of the castle was built in 1813. 5 Victory Museum ( Zafer Müzesi ), Ordu Blv 7 . This museum dedicated to the Turkish War of Independence is closed long-term for rebuilding. ( updated Nov 2022 ) 6 Gedik Ahmet Pasha Imaret Mosque on Kurtuluş Cd is centrepiece of a kulliye , a religious complex with a medrese (seminary), imaret (hospice) and hamam. It was built in 1472 and restored in 1795. The Archaeological Museum at the foot of Kurtuluş Cd has closed down.

pages.caption: VictoryMuseumAfyonkarahsar.JPG · CeeGee · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:VictoryMuseumAfyonkarahsar.JPG
pages.text: It's not known what will become of its extensive collection. 7 Altıgöz Bridge was built in 1209, and is still used by light vehicles. Altıgöz means six eyes or arches. The setting is scrappy and not scenic.

pages.caption: Agadir WV banner.jpg · Gottfried Hoffmann -… · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Agadir_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: Agadir ( Moroccan Arabic : أݣادير) is a city in the southern part of Morocco . Agadir is a tourist resort that is popular with European travelers and Moroccans alike. It has a beach with all the appropriate facilities for beach-tourism . The city is especially attractive, it is clean and orderly with very friendly locals. Agadir is of interest primarily because of its location, as it is surrounded by the Anti Atlas, the Sahara Desert , many natural parks, and secluded beaches which are all easily accessible from Agadir. 1 Agadir-Al Massira Airport ( AGA ) ( 20 km southeast of the city ).

pages.caption: Agadir WV banner.jpg · Gottfried Hoffmann -… · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Agadir_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: Agadir has an international airport with direct flights coming from major cities in Europe as well as many charter flights arriving from all over Europe. If you are flying from the US, Canada, Asia or elsewhere, you'll have to change planes in Casablanca . ( updated Jan 2018 ) Getting there: Official taxi costs 200 dirham plus 20 dirham per each bag. Cheaper taxis can be found just outside of the airport, with prices starting at 80-100 dirham (as of Jan 2018). At the roundabout, just outside the airport territory, you can usually find two or three grand taxis.

pages.caption: Agadir WV banner.jpg · Gottfried Hoffmann -… · CC BY 3.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Agadir_WV_banner.jpg
pages.text: They leave whenever full and go to Inezgane, half way to Agadir. From there you can find another collective taxi to Agadir. There are no direct buses from the airport, however a transit bus #37 can be caught at the main road junction just outside the airport, it goes to Inezgane for 7 dirham every 40 minutes or so. From there you'll need to catch another bus for 4 dirham or grand taxi to Agadir for another 7 dirham (as of Jan 2024).

pages.caption: Aéroport Agadir.jpg · Clément Bardot · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A%C3%A9roport_Agadir.jpg
pages.text: The Alsa bus company launched the airport shuttle between the city center and the airport for 50 dirham one way, and or round-trip for 80 dirham per person, as of Jan 2024. More international connections and ultra low-cost flights from Europe fly to the airport of Marrakesh . From there you can take an intercity bus to Agadir. CTM and Supratours buses depart from this station. There are several daily and direct buses from/to Essaouira (3 hr, 70 dirham), Ouarzazate (6-6.75 hr, 140 dirham), and Marrakech (3.5 hr, 100 dirham). ( updated Apr 2019 )

pages.caption: Aéroport Agadir.jpg · Clément Bardot · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A%C3%A9roport_Agadir.jpg
pages.text: 3 Gare Routière Inezgane ( Inezgane Bus Station ) ( around 10 km from the center ). Inezgane town is the region's bus hub . It serves all the destinations of CTM and Supratours and many more for often a cheaper fare. It is very usual to arrive there, especially when not relying on CTM or Supratours, and not in Agadir center. A city bus to Agadir center goes for 3.50 dirham/person and is convenient and fast (use buses 97, 98 and 99). The grand taxi to Agadir costs from 5 dirham/person.

pages.caption: Aéroport Agadir.jpg · Clément Bardot · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A%C3%A9roport_Agadir.jpg
pages.text: One can go to Inezgane directly from the airport, which is closer, easier to catch buses to Marrakech (3 hr, 70-80 dirham), Ouarzazate , Taroudannt and other places. ( updated Apr 2019 ) Between Essaouira and Agadir it is very easy to catch an intercity bus anywhere along the way. During the day there is one bus about every hour. While CTM and Supratours are not allowed to pick up additional passengers, local intercity buses do not have such a restriction. This is a great way to explore the coast including Taghazout between these two cities without issues. The regular price for the full distance is 50 dirham.

pages.caption: Building Amazigh Culture Museum Agadir.jpg · Abdeaitali · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Building_Amazigh_Culture_Museum_Agadir.jpg
pages.text: The touristy part of the city is small enough to be able to walk it. There is a public bus service which is quite reliable. Fares are usually 3.50-5 dirham, directly paid to the driver, who will hand you a proper ticket. Keep the ticket until the end, there might be controls. Maps can be obtained from the Tourist Office which is along the Boulevard Mohammad V near the Miramar Hotel. Alternatively, also OpenStreetMap has the Agadir bus network available, so get yourself one of the mobile apps using OpenStreetMap, like OsmAnd or Mapy.cz.

pages.caption: Building Amazigh Culture Museum Agadir.jpg · Abdeaitali · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Building_Amazigh_Culture_Museum_Agadir.jpg
pages.text: Most of the Agadir's petit taxi are quite legal and use the taximeter (you can ask the driver to do it without any problems). If you go around the center though, they will ask you normally from 30 to 50 dirham (as of 2019). This is not legal, and you can refuse to pay anything but the price listed on the taximeter if it has been reset at the beginning of the trip. Mopeds can be rented around Hotel Kenzi, but they are expensive, more than 100 dirham an hour. 1 Museum Municipal du Patrimoine Amazigh , Avenue Hassan II , ☏ +212 5288-21632 .

pages.caption: Building Amazigh Culture Museum Agadir.jpg · Abdeaitali · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Credits: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Building_Amazigh_Culture_Museum_Agadir.jpg
pages.text: The museum which exhibits a small collection of Berber objects from 18th and 19th century the likes of old Berber music instruments, Berber jewelry, traditional clothing and old manuscripts. ( updated Oct 2017 ) 2 Memory of Agadir Museum ( Corner of the Avenue des F.A.R. and Avenue President Kennedy ).
